Pascua Yaqui Tribe Opens Casino Del Sol's New Vahi Taa'am Property in Tucson

Published November 15, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

The Pascua Yaqui Tribe opens Vahi Taa'am today, a new Casino Del Sol property at 1055 W. Grant Road in Tucson, Arizona — the tribe's third casino and, according to the Arizona Daily Star, the first one located inside Tucson's actual city limits. A ribbon-cutting and remarks are planned for the morning, with the property opening to the public in the afternoon and a fireworks show set for 8 p.m.

What's inside

Vahi Taa'am — which the tribe says means "three sons" in the Yoeme language — includes a 52,525-square-foot gaming floor with 928 slot machines and 24 table games, plus a sportsbook, two restaurants, a food court and five bars, inside a roughly 153,480-square-foot building. A domed ceiling section spans 24,000 square feet and features a mural by local artist Joe Pagac, and the property's interior centerpiece is a sculpture titled "Aniam Yo'orine (Respect the World)" by Marcelino C. Flores III. The tribe says the property expects to create up to 500 new jobs across gaming, food and beverage, hospitality, security and administration.

A 15-year path to opening day

The project traces back roughly 15 years, when the tribe purchased the shuttered Century Park 16 movie theater on the site without announcing specific plans for it. Because federal law generally requires tribal land to be held in trust for a casino to operate there, the tribe began that process in 2019, and the city of Tucson separately approved an intergovernmental agreement that would apply once the parcel became part of the Yaqui Reservation. The late Rep. Raúl Grijalva introduced the federal legislation to place the land into trust in 2022, which President Biden signed that year, clearing the way for construction. Demolition of the old theater began in 2023, followed by roughly three years of building work ahead of today's opening.

What comes next

Tribal officials are reportedly studying a future convention center and resort hotel on the site, and the tribe says it's working with businesses along a stretch of Grant Road to vacate properties for later phases of the project. For now, Vahi Taa'am becomes the Pascua Yaqui Tribe's third gaming property in the Tucson area, alongside its existing Casino Del Sol and Casino of the Sun locations outside the city's boundaries — giving the tribe a gaming and sports betting footprint now anchored, for the first time, inside Tucson proper.
